certificate: CEA Certificate in Content Creation — issued on successful completion of the full content package (planned, shot, edited and published material with captions) A smartphone with a camera, free CapCut, free Canva, free YouTube/TikTok/Instagram accounts, and academy computers Document status Approved for delivery — Version 1.0, October 2026 About this document. This is the master design document for the CEA Content Creation course. It explains why the course exists, who it is for, what a graduate can do, how the nine sessions are organised, how learners are assessed, and what they must produce to earn the certificate. Session-by-session teaching notes live in the companion folder Part2_Session_Materials . Instructors should read this document in full before teaching Session 1. 1. toolset: A smartphone with a camera, free CapCut, free Canva, free YouTube/TikTok/Instagram accounts, and academy
tools: A smartphone with a camera, free CapCut, free Canva, free YouTube/TikTok/Instagram accounts, and academy
audience: This course is designed for absolute beginners. The typical learner is one or more of the following
School leavers who want a practical, income-earning skill they can use immediately
NYSC corps members who want to support a business, a church, or build a personal brand during service
Small-business owners and staff — shop owners, tailors, salon owners, restaurant cooks, barbers — who need to promote their own business but cannot pay an agency
Church media volunteers who record services, events and announcements and want their output to look and sound better
Aspiring freelancers who want to offer social media management or content services to local clients
Social media managers and virtual assistants who post for others but have never had formal training
Personal brand builders — comedians, faith creators, students, fitness coaches — who post on TikTok, Instagram or YouTube
entry_requirements: There is no formal academic entry requirement. To join and benefit fully, a learner needs
A smartphone with a working camera. Android or iPhone both work. The phone should be able to record at least 1080p video (almost all phones made in the last several years can)
At least 8 GB of free storage on the phone (or access to an academy computer for editing) so that footage can be stored and edited
A free CapCut account/app installed on the phone or available on an academy computer
A free Canva account (email sign-up is enough)
Free YouTube, TikTok or Instagram accounts for publishing practice. A learner may use any one of these; they do not need
problem: Content Creation is a practical, beginner-level course that turns a learner who only watches videos on their phone into someone who can plan, shoot, edit and publish their own content for a small business, a church, a personal brand or a client. The course is built around doing, not listening. From the very first session, learners are making decisions about their audience, standing up to shoot with their phones, and editing real clips in free software.
